hard_cap_triggered.rule: Design introduces circular dependencies or creates a distributed monolith (D1 <= 10)
Design provides no API contracts (just endpoint names without request/response schemas) (D2 <= 8)
Design has no database schema or only lists table names without fields/types/relationships (D3 <= 8)
Design completely ignores the existing system context (D4 <= 8)

dimension_1.justification: Clean separation of concerns strictly adhering to the existing layered microservice architecture (Model → Repository → Service → API). Layer dependencies are strictly unidirectional with zero circular references. The modular extraction of ContentValidator and Celery background tasks appropriately isolates business rules and external I/O. Concurrency control via PostgreSQL transaction advisory locks correctly addresses race conditions across horizontally scaled service instances without introducing unnecessary distributed locking infrastructure.

dimension_2.justification: Exemplary RESTful API design. All endpoints feature exhaustive Pydantic v2 request/response schemas with explicit types, regex domain validators, and length bounds. List endpoints properly incorporate pagination metadata (page, page_size, total, total_pages). Appropriate HTTP verbs and granular status codes (201, 403, 404, 409, 422) are documented with exact semantics. Auth requirements and role-based permissions (Creator vs Brand) are explicitly specified per endpoint, and error formatting aligns directly with the existing AppError standard.

dimension_3.justification: Comprehensive and robust data model covering all required entities (content_submissions, content_versions, and content_drafts). Foreign keys and cardinality constraints are properly modeled, including a critical compound UNIQUE index on (submission_id, version_number) ensuring sequence integrity. Standard audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at) and soft-delete mixins match existing repository conventions, and the SubmissionStatus enum fully captures the required submission lifecycle.

dimension_4.justification: Flawless adherence to existing system context and constraints. The design integrates cleanly with existing User, Campaign, and Application repositories, reuses existing Celery/PostgreSQL/Redis infrastructure, and respects the X-User-Id header auth model. Every integration boundary includes rigorous failure handling: fail-open with warnings for missing sensitive word dictionaries, 10-second client timeouts with Celery retries and incomplete_checks flags for the external Image Quality API, and SSRF mitigations for CDN validation.

dimension_5.justification: Outstanding architectural decision-making and risk analysis. Five key technical decisions (synchronous v1 validation chain, append-only version table, advisory locking, pre-uploaded CDN URLs, and UTC deadline enforcement) are thoroughly justified with concrete alternatives considered, rationale, and acknowledged trade-offs. Four high- and medium-severity production risks are identified with actionable, multi-faceted mitigations.

scores.overall_assessment: This is an exemplary, production-grade technical design that meticulously fulfills all functional and non-functional requirements while seamlessly fitting into the existing FastAPI/SQLAlchemy microservice architecture. It strikes an optimal balance between pragmatic v1 execution and robust engineering safeguards such as transactional concurrency control, immutable versioning, and resilient integration failure modes.

dimension_1.justification: The design exhibits a clean, unidirectional layered architecture (Router -> Service -> Repository -> Model) with well-defined module boundaries and high cohesion. Responsibilities are strictly segregated: ReviewService encapsulates state machine validation and concurrency guards, ReviewRepository handles async SQLAlchemy queries and row locking, and Celery workers handle background SLA sweeps. Horizontal scalability is well addressed via Redis claim locking and post-commit Celery notification dispatches without circular dependencies.

dimension_2.justification: RESTful conventions are followed rigorously. Every endpoint specifies detailed request and response schemas using Pydantic v2 with explicit types, field lengths, and validation rules. Proper HTTP verbs and status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409) are paired with standardized error structures. List endpoints implement generic PaginatedResponse[T], authentication and role-based authorization are defined per endpoint, and critical operational flows (distributed compliance claiming, revision limit overrides) have explicit contracts.

dimension_3.justification: The data model is complete and production-grade. Entities (reviews, review_comments, review_audit_log) include all necessary columns, constraints, foreign keys, cascades, and enums. Query access patterns are supported by targeted indexes, notably a PostgreSQL partial unique index ensuring at most one active review cycle per stage. The model thoughtfully harmonizes platform constraints (inheriting Base, TimestampMixin, SoftDeleteMixin) with append-only immutability requirements for audit trails.

dimension_4.justification: The design adheres to all constraints and seamlessly integrates with existing services. It properly utilizes Base, TimestampMixin, and SoftDeleteMixin, registers endpoints under /api/v1/, enforces auth via X-User-Id header and require_role() dependencies, uses PostgreSQL SELECT FOR UPDATE for row-level concurrency, and ensures Celery notifications are fire-and-forget via post-commit hooks. Interface contracts, failure handling, and backward compatibility are explicitly detailed for all six neighboring services.

dimension_5.justification: The design provides an outstanding trade-off analysis across six foundational technical decisions, evaluating multiple concrete alternatives, justifications, and performance implications for each. Furthermore, it identifies four realistic production risks (lock contention, abandoned compliance leases, Celery broker failure, and XSS injection) and supplies effective mitigations including distributed lock TTLs, bleach sanitization, and late task acknowledgment.

scores.overall_assessment: This is an exemplary, production-ready technical design document that thoroughly fulfills all domain requirements, edge cases, and platform constraints. It demonstrates deep architectural rigor with robust concurrency controls, meticulous schema design, and pragmatic trade-off analysis.
